report:
## Ivermectin and COVID-19 Mortality: What the Evidence Shows

The answer is **no** — rigorous evidence does not support ivermectin reducing COVID-19 death risk, despite some earlier, lower-quality studies suggesting otherwise.

**Early meta-analyses were mixed but weak.** Some pooled analyses (e.g., a 2021 review in *Pharmacological Reports*) suggested a mortality benefit, but a companion analysis noted this benefit came with "low certainty of evidence" (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187140212100206X). These early meta-analyses often included small, methodologically flawed, or later-retracted trials, which inflated apparent benefits.

**The largest, most rigorous randomized trial found no benefit.** The TOGETHER trial, a large placebo-controlled RCT published in the *New England Journal of Medicine*, found ivermectin did **not** reduce hospitalization or COVID-19 progression compared to placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).

**Updated systematic reviews confirm no mortality benefit.** A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis (PubMed) concluded ivermectin did not significantly improve critical outcomes including mortality, ICU admission, or ventilator use (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38510038/).

**Major health authorities agree.** The World Health Organization, after reviewing accumulated trial evidence, updated its guidelines in November 2023 to **strongly recommend against** using ivermectin for COVID-19, citing lack of evidence and biological implausibility (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic). The FDA has similarly stated that available clinical trial data do not demonstrate ivermectin's effectiveness against COVID-19.

**Conclusion:** While a handful of early, low-quality meta-analyses suggested possible mortality benefits, higher-quality, large-scale RCTs and updated systematic reviews — along with WHO and FDA assessments — consistently find no significant reduction in COVID-19 mortality from ivermectin.
